title: South Carolina's 7th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: South Carolina's 7th Congressional District covers the Grand Strand and Pee Dee regions, anchored in fast-growing Horry County. Incumbent Republican Russell Fry, first elected in 2022 after defeating Rep. Tom Rice in a primary fueled by Rice's impeachment vote, is seeking a third term. The district is heavily Republican (Cook Political Rating: Solid R) and hasn't elected a Democrat to Congress in the modern era. Democratic challenger John Vincent, a retired Navy command master chief and small business owner, is campaigning on economic populism and bipartisanship, but faces a steep uphill climb in a district where Fry won 65% of the vote in 2024.
polling_note: No public general election opinion polls were found for this race as of July 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican'.

candidates.name: Russell Fry
candidates.summary: Russell Fry is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after defeating Rep. Tom Rice in the Republican primary and winning the general election with 65% of the vote. He previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2015 to 2022, where he was Majority Chief Whip, and worked as an attorney along the Grand Strand. Fry, a close ally of President Donald Trump who received Trump's endorsement in 2022, serves on the House Judiciary Committee and was elected president of the congressional freshman class.

candidates.name: John Vincent
candidates.summary: John Vincent is a retired U.S. Navy command master chief petty officer and first-time candidate running for Congress in South Carolina's 7th District. He served 20 years in the Navy, including being stationed at Charleston Naval Base, and later worked as a sales manager for WBTW-TV in Florence before starting a leadership consulting firm. Vincent campaigns on economic populism, supporting a $15 minimum wage, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, and a woman's right to choose up to 14 weeks, while emphasizing bipartisanship and his slogan 'Common Sense Over Chaos'.

forecast.rationale: There are no public general-election polls for this race. The forecast relies on structural factors: Cook Political Report rates the district 'Solid Republican,' the district has not elected a Democrat to Congress in the modern era, and incumbent Russell Fry won 65% of the vote in 2024. Democratic challenger John Vincent is a credible nominee with a compelling personal story, but faces an extremely difficult partisan environment in this heavily Republican district. The absence of polling reduces confidence from high to medium, but the available race data points to an overwhelming Republican advantage.
